para: The construction is most transparent in the four-fold family generated from Gentzen's intuitionistic sequent calculus LJ. In LJ, the right-hand side of every sequent is restricted to contain at most one formula; this is the syntactic encoding of the constructive reading of disjunction and existence, under which a disjunction is only asserted when one of its disjuncts has been established. Dualizing the right restriction to the left yields a calculus in which the left-hand side of every sequent contains at most one formula: this is Rauszer's dual-intuitionistic logic, here written LDJ, whose provable sequents correspond to the theorems of the co-Heyting algebra. A second, independent duality operation exchanges the treatment of the implication connective: the result is the counter-intuitionistic calculus CoLJ. Combining both operations produces the fourth member of the orbit, which collapses back to a variant of classical logic when both restrictions are simultaneously lifted, confirming that LK itself is a fixed point of the combined duality and that the orbit of LJ under the Klein four-group is genuinely four-element. The same construction, applied to Sambin's Basic Logic and to the Ardeshir–Vaezian calculus U, populates further regions of the graph with calculi whose positions would otherwise require independent discovery.
